summary: VAPID lets an application server voluntarily identify itself to a push service. A signed token in a vapid authentication scheme tells the push service who is sending, which helps with restricting abuse and contacting the sender if needed.

eli5.summary: The sender shows a signed name tag to the delivery service, so the service knows who sent the notification and who to call about problems.

questions: how to identify an application server to a push service
what is vapid in web push
how to restrict a push subscription to one server
subtitle: How a Web Push application server can optionally sign its requests so a push service knows who is calling.

tldr.problem: A push service cannot know an application server in advance, so it has little basis for telling legitimate push requests from bogus ones, and anyone holding a subscription URI can send to it.
tldr.mechanism: The application server signs a JSON Web Token with an ECDSA P-256 key and sends it, with its public key, in an Authorization header using the new "vapid" scheme. A subscription can also be restricted to that public key.
tldr.outcome: The push service gets a stable identity, optional contact details and a way to limit a subscription to one application server. It remains voluntary, and contact details are unvalidated.

today: RFC 8292 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Servers Identify Themselves
sections.content:
The Web Push protocol (RFC 8030) lets an application server ask a push service to deliver a message to a user agent. By design, the push service does not know the application server beforehand, and RFC 8030 defines no mandatory authentication, partly to protect privacy.

The cost is a higher risk of denial-of-service attacks, because the push service has little to tell legitimate requests from bogus ones. There is a second problem: anyone who learns a push message subscription URI can send messages to that user agent.

The Voluntary Application Server Identification (VAPID) method lets a server volunteer a stable identity and, if it wants, contact details such as an email address. A push service can use a consistent identity to establish behavioral expectations and trigger exception handling when a server deviates. The RFC notes that contacting an operator has proven valuable when software errors cause large jumps in push volume.
sections.eli5: A mail room takes parcels from strangers. If a sender shows who they are, the mail room can spot a sudden flood of parcels and phone the sender to ask what is going on.

sections.title: Self-Identification with a Signed Token
sections.content:
An application server that wants to identify itself generates and keeps a signing key pair. The key pair MUST be usable with the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) over the P-256 curve. When requesting delivery, the server includes a JSON Web Token (JWT) signed with that key. The JWT MUST use a JSON Web Signature, with the algorithm identified as ES256.

The token carries these claims:

  • aud (Audience) MUST be the Unicode serialization of the origin of the push resource URL. This binds the token to one push service and lets it be reused for every push resource URL sharing that origin.
  • exp (Expiry) MUST be present and MUST NOT be more than 24 hours after the request. The limit balances reuse against the cost and likelihood of token theft.
  • sub (Subject) is optional. It SHOULD hold a contact URI, either mailto: or https:.

Additional claims are allowed, but because the token travels in a header field they SHOULD be kept small. A push service MAY reject a request with a 403 (Forbidden) status if the signature or claims are invalid, and MUST NOT use information from an invalid token.
sections.eli5: The sender writes a note, signs it with a special pen only they own, and says when the note stops being good. The note says which delivery company it is for and can include a phone number.

sections.title: The vapid Authentication Scheme
sections.content:
The RFC defines a new HTTP authentication scheme named vapid. Credentials carry the signed JWT plus the key that signed it, in two parameters:

  • t holds the JWT.
  • k holds the application server's ECDSA public key in uncompressed X9.62 form, base64url encoded.

X9.62 encoding was chosen over a JSON Web Key because a JWK has no canonical form, which makes comparing keys from different sources harder, and because X9.62 is considerably smaller. Unknown or unsupported parameters MUST be ignored, and the realm parameter is ignored. A challenge for the scheme contains only the scheme name, and no parameters are currently defined.

The scheme is for origin-server authentication only. It MUST NOT be used with the Proxy-Authenticate or Proxy-Authorization header fields. Using a different scheme is how the signature algorithm or other parameters would be updated, so existing scheme negotiation works without new parameter negotiation.

One key rule: an application server MUST use a different private key for message encryption (RFC 8291) than for signing the token. A push service SHOULD reject a message whose two values are identical with a 400 (Bad Request) status.
sections.eli5: The note and a copy of the sender's public stamp go in two labeled boxes on the parcel. The sender must not use the same stamp for sealing the parcel and for signing the note.

sections.title: Restricting a Subscription
sections.content:
The application server's public key is a stable identifier, so it can lock a push message subscription to that server. This reduces reliance on keeping the subscription URI secret.

To create a restricted subscription, the user agent adds a body to the subscription request. The body is a JSON object with a vapid member holding the P-256 public key in uncompressed form, base64url encoded. Its media type is application/webpush-options+json. A push service MUST ignore a body of any other media type, and MUST ignore members of the object that it does not understand.

After that, every delivery request to the subscription MUST carry a JWT signed by the matching private key. A push service MUST reject a message with missing or invalid vapid authentication, and might use 401 (Unauthorized) when it is absent and 403 (Forbidden) when it is invalid. Authentication is invalid if:

  • the token or public key is missing,
  • the signature does not verify with the included key,
  • the time is later than exp or more than 24 hours before it,
  • the origin of the push resource is not in aud, or
  • the signing key differs from the one used when the subscription was created.

A push service MUST NOT forward the JWT or public key to the user agent. To change its signing key, a server must have the user agent create a new subscription restricted to the new key, so servers need to remember which key each subscription used.
sections.eli5: A family can tell the post office that only one particular shop may send to their mailbox. Any parcel without that shop's valid signed note is turned away.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The scheme is vulnerable to replay attacks if an attacker acquires a valid JWT. Sending requests over HTTPS, as RFC 8030 requires, provides confidentiality, and narrow limits on how long a token can be reused cap the value of a stolen one.

Contact information is unproven. A server can claim any email address or contact URI, so a push service operator cannot use unvalidated contact information in any security-critical decision.

Checking a signature takes a non-trivial amount of computation, which is not ideal when identifying legitimate requests during a denial-of-service attack. Application servers are therefore encouraged to reuse tokens, so the push service can cache validation results.

Changing the signing key breaks linkability between messages sent under different keys, and a push service might categorize requests under a new key differently. Migrating gradually reduces the chance that the new key is treated as abusive.
sections.eli5: If someone steals a signed note they can reuse it until it expires, so notes expire quickly. A phone number on the note might be fake, so the mail room must not trust it too much.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The document registers the vapid scheme in the HTTP Authentication Scheme Registry. It also creates a "VAPID Authentication Scheme Parameters" registry under the "Web Push Parameters" grouping, using the Specification Required policy. The registry starts with t (JWT authentication token) and k (signing key), both for the Authorization header field.

Finally, it registers the application/webpush-options+json media type, intended for LIMITED USE with the Web Push protocol.
sections.eli5: The RFC adds its new names to the official lists so nobody else uses them for something different.

Reasons a restricted subscription rejects a request

items.title: Missing
items.text: No token or no public key in the request.

items.title: Bad signature
items.text: The JWT does not verify with the included key.

items.title: Wrong time
items.text: Past exp, or more than 24 hours before exp.

items.title: Wrong audience
items.text: The push resource origin is not in aud.

items.title: Wrong key
items.text: The key differs from the one used at subscription time.
